method: Manual browser inspection of the public Vivid Media/Matterport viewer: launch, dollhouse, floorplan, and interior views. No model geometry or private assets extracted.
scope: Six example suites/rooms. Observations apply only to the scanned sample; room numbers, capture dates, dimensions, current furniture specifications, and representativeness across each hall are unverified.
screenshotsUsage: Saved locally as visual audit references. Provider attribution retained. These are not permission to republish provider imagery.

records.observedTitle: Gray Court Double Rooms with Suite Bath
verifiedLayoutFeatures: Two separate bedrooms, each furnished with two beds, appear in the scanned suite.
Bedrooms sit on opposite sides of a central connecting bathroom zone.
Bedroom interior shows desks with upper shelving, desk chairs, drawers/dressers, and raised bed frames with storage beneath.
Windows and a wall-mounted heating/cooling unit occupy the exterior bedroom wall.
An open center circulation area is visible between bedroom furniture.
uncertainties: Bathroom fixture boundaries are not fully resolved by the saved overhead view.
Exact room numbers, dimensions, door swings, closet boundaries, and allowed bed heights are unverified.
No dedicated living room is visible in the sample; this does not establish absence of hall-wide lounge spaces.
plannerImplications: Treat each bedroom as a separate editable room; do not flatten the entire suite into one furniture area.
Keep the central bathroom connection and bedroom entry circulation clear.
Model window/HVAC wall as a fixed obstruction once measured; do not treat under-bed storage as extra floor area.
Do not assume the two bedrooms have identical dimensions.
quizImplications: This sample supports explaining suite-bath sharing and bedroom-based hosting, not a hall social-vibe rating.

records.observedTitle: Keller Hall Double with Private Bath
verifiedLayoutFeatures: One bedroom furnished with two beds is visible.
The footprint has an entry recess and a projecting bay-window area rather than a plain rectangle.
An enclosed bathroom area with visible toilet and shower lies beside the entrance.
Interior view shows a built-in closet opening with hanging rail and shelf.
The bedroom has a heater below the bay window, carpet, and wooden bed/drawer furniture.
titleDerivedFeatures: The scanned double is described as having a private bath; private refers to the room, not a single occupant.
uncertainties: Bathroom sharing beyond the provider title is not independently confirmed.
Exact closet dimensions and which exterior doors connect to the corridor are unverified.
Exact dimensions, room number, and current furniture inventory are unknown.
plannerImplications: Preserve bay-window, bathroom, and entry recess geometry; a bounding rectangle would create false usable space.
Add fixed closet and window/heater zones before moving furniture.
Keep bathroom/closet/entry access clear.
quizImplications: Distinguish sharing a bedroom from sharing a bathroom across multiple rooms; a private-bath double is not a private bedroom.

verifiedLayoutFeatures: Two adjacent bedrooms each contain two beds in the scan.
A tiled connecting passage runs beside both bedrooms.
The passage connects to separate fixture areas at its ends, including a visible toilet and a shower area.
Vanities/sinks and mirrors are visible both along the connecting passage and through a separate doorway in the interior view.
Bedroom doors open from the shared connecting area; furniture is placed around the bedroom perimeter.
uncertainties: The title does not give exact room numbers.
Fixture access rules, lock operation, and whether the scan represents all suite configurations are not established.
No dimensions or permitted furniture arrangements measured.
plannerImplications: Treat shared tiled bath/circulation area as fixed geometry, not additional bedroom space.
Preserve separate bedroom doors and bathroom compartment access.
Keep furniture layouts local to each bedroom unless the full suite is explicitly modeled.
quizImplications: Show the actual bathroom arrangement as an example; do not call the tiled connecting passage a living room or hosting area.

verifiedLayoutFeatures: The saved overhead view shows two beds in the left bedroom and one bed in the right bedroom.
The two bedrooms are separated by a central bathroom zone.
A central sink/vanity compartment is visually separate from an adjoining compartment containing a toilet and shower.
Bedroom footprints have entry-side recesses rather than forming two uninterrupted rectangles.
The single-bedroom interior shows a bed, desk with shelving, dresser under a window, a door toward the bath, and another closed door.
titleDerivedFeatures: Provider labels the sample single/double suite.
uncertainties: Room numbers are not established. This tour is NOT verified as planner room North0013.
Exact closet boundaries are not established; entry-side recesses must not be labeled closets without further evidence.
Door-to-corridor versus door-to-closet mapping is not fully verified.
Dimensions, furnishing rules, and all other North Court room configurations remain unknown.
plannerImplications: Keep single and double bedrooms distinct in geometry, furnishing counts, and privacy descriptions.
Represent the bath as separate fixed compartments between bedrooms.
Do not insert North0013 dimensions or outline into this sample, or this sample furnishing into North0013, without room matching.
Future modeling requires door/closet measurements and clearance checks; preserve irregular entry recesses now as unknown areas rather than usable rectangles.
quizImplications: Separate own-bedroom preference from suite-bath sharing; this sample shows that a single bedroom can still be part of a shared suite.
Avoid scoring all North rooms as private bedrooms.

records.observedTitle: South Court Double Rooms with Suite Bath
verifiedLayoutFeatures: The scanned suite has two bedrooms with two beds visible in each.
A central bathroom zone lies between the bedrooms.
The overhead view shows a toilet and sink in the upper bathroom compartment and a separate shower footprint below.
Each room has desks, chairs, drawer units, windows, and an open middle circulation area.
The bedroom outlines have different entry-side recesses; they are not obviously identical rectangles.
uncertainties: Exact closet boundaries and every door swing are unresolved.
Room numbers, dimensions, capture date, and current assignment rules are not established by the tour.
No dedicated living room is visible in this sample; hall lounge provision not audited.
plannerImplications: Model bathroom and entry recesses as fixed geometry.
Do not mirror one bedroom outline automatically to create the other.
Check that bed and desk arrangements preserve routes to bathroom and bedroom entrance.
quizImplications: This supports describing a suite bathroom between double bedrooms; it does not establish the social atmosphere of South Court.

verifiedLayoutFeatures: The overhead scan shows one bed in the left bedroom and two in the right bedroom.
A shared tiled area connects the bedroom doors and bathroom fixtures.
Toilet/shower compartment lies off the shared area; a separate sink is visible at the lower edge of the overhead view.
Bedroom footprints include entry-side recesses and doorways; the single and double have distinct outlines.
Desks, chairs, bed frames, drawers, and windows appear in the furnished bedrooms.
uncertainties: Exact room numbers, capture date, dimensions, and lock/access arrangements are not verified.
Some dark or missing areas in the scanned footprint may be scan gaps, not architectural voids.
No standalone living room is visible in the scanned sample; common rooms elsewhere not audited.
plannerImplications: Model distinct single and double spaces plus fixed shared bath/circulation geometry.
Do not count tiled bathroom circulation as optional hosting area.
Do not trace black scan gaps as walls without matching official floorplans.
Preserve door access when proposing furniture layouts.
quizImplications: Own-bedroom privacy and bathroom-sharing preference should be separate questions.
Offer the sample tour for students to judge layout rather than assigning a personality to the entire hall.
